title: fix(cuda-graph): restore shape-guarded warmup for capture/replay regression
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: This PR fixes a regression introduced by recent CUDA graph capture/replay changes where warmup runs were incorrectly using unguarded kernels for some dynamic-shape workloads. The regression caused higher-latency first requests and occasional correctness issues when the runtime replayed captured graphs for requests whose sequence length or batch-size diverged from the graph's shape guard expectations. Motivation: CUDA graph capture/replay is a key optimization for steady-state latency on long-running sequences. During the refactor that moved shape-guard evaluation into the capture pipeline we inadvertently skipped evaluating shape guards during warmup for the replay path. That allowed captures to proceed with an incompatible kernel selection in a subset of cases (variable batch sizes and prefix-cache hits), causing either wasted re-captures or incorrect KV-cache handling. Changes: - runtime/cuda_graph_manager.cpp: Re-introduce explicit shape-guard evaluation during warmup path for replay. Add checks to ensure that a captured graph is only reused when guards match request shape and cache state. - runtime/kv_cache.cpp: Add lightweight cache-state fingerprint used by shape-guard comparison to avoid deep KV comparisons on hot paths. - runtime/kernel_selector.cpp: Minor guard evaluation helpers extracted for reuse between capture/warmup/replay flows. - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp: Ensure warmup orchestration waits for guard confirmation before marking a graph as reusable. - tests/gpu/cuda_graph_warmup_test.cpp: New unit + integration test covering dynamic batch sizes, prefix caching, and replay reuse. - perf-canary/configs/cuda-graph-warmup.yaml: Canary job added to detect regressions in capture/replay warmup latency. Commits: - a3f9b4d: squash: fix: evaluate shape guards in warmup for replay path - f2b1c8e: test: add integration test for dynamic batch warmup/replay - 9d6e2a4: perf: add canary config and CI job - 7c1b5f0: docs: note behavior in runtime capture docs Files changed (high-level): - runtime/cuda_graph_manager.cpp: rework warmup path and guard checks (key logic) - runtime/kv_cache.cpp/h: add fingerprint helper and lightweight state accessors - runtime/kernel_selector.cpp/h: extracted guard helpers - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp: gating logic to wait for guard confirmation - tests/gpu/cuda_graph_warmup_test.cpp: new tests, uses small model fixture - perf-canary/configs/cuda-graph-warmup.yaml: new canary job - docs/runtime/cuda_graph.md: documentation update Notes on approach: - The fix is intentionally conservative: we check both tensor shape signatures and a small KV-cache fingerprint (first/last token presence + cached length) before reusing a graph. This avoids expensive KV comparisons while preventing mismatches that previously caused re-captures or incorrect outputs. - Added extensive unit/integration tests to cover boundary cases (batch size changes, zero-prefix cache, partial cache hits). - Performance: Microbenchmarks show warmup overhead increased by ~0.7ms on the worst synthetic short-seq cases but steady-state latency improves because we avoid frequent re-captures; canary results included in CI. Validation and CI: - CI matrix includes GPU unit tests and a perf canary run. First CI run failed (shape-guard test) due to a missing fence in the warmup waiter; the failing test reproduced locally. - Fix applied (commit 9d6e2a4 -> added guard fence) and CI re-run passed. - Canary run shows no regression vs baseline and eliminates the previous replay-related latency spikes. Checklist: - [x] Add guard checks to warmup/replay path - [x] Add KV cache fingerprint helper - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add perf canary - [x] Documentation update - [x] CI green Review highlights (excerpted): - Arjun Singh: "Good catch — the replay path skipping guards explains the spike we saw in canary 2026-02-04. Two requests: 1) Can we ensure the fingerprinting code is bounded CPU-wise? 2) Add a short comment in cuda_graph.md describing the guard semantics." - Maya (author): "Answered: fingerprint is constant-time (O(1) fields) and uses cached offset read; added comment to docs in second commit." - Lena Cho: "Tests look good. One nit: rename has_compatible_cache -> cache_fingerprint_matches for clarity." - Maya: "Renamed helper and updated tests." - Diego Marquez: "Approvals after CI pass. Consider a follow-up to extend canary to simulate multi-tenant mixes." Risk and roll-out: - Low-risk change to warmup logic, behaviour conservative and guarded by tests + canary. No config flips required. We added a canary monitoring job to catch future regressions. Release notes: "Fix regression in CUDA graph capture/replay warmup where shape guards could be skipped leading to re-captures or incorrect replay reuse; improves stability for dynamic batch and KV-cache workloads." Merge: Merged via squash-and-merge after CI green and approvals. Root cause references: ENG-3980 (refactor that moved guard evaluation), incident SUP-1142 (customer incident reporting spikes).
